question: The HCF and the LCM of two numbers are 29 and 174, respectively. If one of the numbers is 58, find the other one.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Product of numbers = **HCF** × **LCM**

Other number = (29 × 174) ÷ 58

Other number = 174 ÷ 2 = 87

**∴ The correct answer is 87.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**HCF** = 29

**LCM** = 174

**First Number (n₁)** = 58

**Formula Used:**

n₁ × n₂ = HCF × LCM

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c3ff1df27534bf6186e2e39e3e691026fb4f351271dcc93d4abe53866c6073db.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 58 × n₂ = 29 × 174

⇒ n₂ = (29 × 174) ÷ 58

⇒ n₂ = 5046 ÷ 58

⇒ n₂ = 87

**∴ The correct answer is 87.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Co-prime Numbers

Two numbers are said to be **co-prime** if their **HCF** is 1. Example: (8, 15).

Relation for Three Numbers

Note that the product rule (n₁×n₂ = HCF×LCM) **does not apply** to more than two numbers.

LCM and HCF Property

The **LCM** of any set of numbers is always exactly divisible by their **HCF**.</p
